notes: Volume V–Z of the collection: 50 pages, 40 entries (5 under V, 30 under W, 3 under Y, 2 under Z) covering architects, builders, a developer, landscape architects, a housing advocate and five firms, read end to end — the title page, the four letter indexes, every entry, every 'Projects in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. The last of the eight letter-range PDFs; the collection is now read in full. Ten entries yielded no numbered San Francisco address: Helen Van Pelt, Leland and Adele Wharton Vaughan, Peter Walker, Rebecca Wood Esherick Watkin, Elizabeth Hillier Tarris Witkin, Catherine Bauer Wurster and Worley Wong have no numbered San Francisco work here; Fred Woods heads an empty list; and M. J. Welch's only entry is 'the 1100 block of Tennessee Street'. Three entries carry a full biography the index never lists — Dorothy Wormser Coblentz, Wright, Rushforth and Cahill, and Wurster, Bernardi and Emmons — the mirror of the trap volumes J–L and P–R hit from the other direction.

coverage.remaining: Nothing. The eight-volume collection is read in full.
coverage.note: 132 numbered-address mentions across 50 pages became 96 findings. 82 reached a parcel, 1 was rejected as a building the volume marks destroyed, and 13 never resolved: 4 numbers the city no longer has, 3 recorded ranges now split across parcels, 2 condominiums, 2 located only as 1 Maritime Plaza or a pair of cross streets, 1 street the register does not hold (30 Craigmont Drive — EAS has no Craigmont in the city), and 1 address EAS holds that no active parcel does. The decline rate is the highest of the eight volumes: 37 of 82 resolved findings were already carried by a survey or statement that documented the building first, most of them the Modern Architecture and Landscape Design statement's Wurster and WBE houses and the Russian Hill inventory's Wright, Rushforth and Cahill flats.
